title: Fix smbd panic when closing files on FUSE filesystems after deletion
description:
This is a patch imported directly from the samba folks.

Fixes LP: #2166678.

Samba's `smbd` can hit an assertion failure when closing a file that has been deleted on a FUSE filesystem. In particular, `vfs_stat_fsp()` can fail after the unlink, leaving the file descriptor in a state that causes `fd_handle_destructor()` to assert.

This imports the upstream fixes for Samba Bug ​15527 (https://bugzilla.samba.org/show_bug.cgi?id=15527):

* Simplify handling of a failing `fstat()` after unlinking a file by clearing `fsp_flags.fstat_before_close`.
* Ensure the file descriptor is reset even when `vfs_stat_fsp()` fails while closing the file handle.

The fixes have been tested on Ubuntu Noble with a mergerfs/FUSE-backed Samba share. Before the fix, deleting a file from SKYBOX VR caused `smbd` to hit the `fd_handle_destructor()` assertion and SKYBOX reported "Error Deleting File", although the file was actually removed. With the patches applied, the same deletion succeeds normally.

The patches are unchanged upstream fixes for Samba Bug ​15527.
commit_message: Fix smbd panic when closing files on FUSE filesystems after deletion

--- a/debian/changelog

@@ -1,3 +1,11 @@
+samba (2:4.19.5+dfsg-4ubuntu9.8) noble; urgency=medium
+
+  * d/p/fail-close-file-handle-reset-fd.patch,
+    d/p/simplify-handling-of-failing-fstat-after-unlinking-file:
+    Fix smbd panic when closing files on FUSE filesystems (LP: #2166678).
+
+ -- Mike Ratcliffe <michael@ratcliffefamily.org>  Wed, 09 Sep 2026 14:45:00 +0100
+
 samba (2:4.19.5+dfsg-4ubuntu9.7) noble-security; urgency=medium
 
   * SECURITY UPDATE: unexpected / directory permissions change
diff --git a/debian/patches/fail-close-file-handle-reset-fd.patch b/debian/patches/fail-close-file-handle-reset-fd.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e219a43
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/fail-close-file-handle-reset-fd.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+Description: s3/smbd: If we fail to close file_handle ensure we should
+ reset the fd
+Author: Noel Power <noel.power@suse.com>
+Bug: https://bugzilla.samba.org/show_bug.cgi?id=15527
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/samba/+bug/2166678
+Origin: upstream, https://github.com/samba-team/samba/commit/0ac741b5705b7e0801a7ec5355d0f9be21e024c6
+Last-Update: 2026-09-24
+
+if fsp_flags.fstat_before_close == true then close_file_smb will call
+vfs_stat which can fail. If it does fail then the fd associated
+with the file handle will still be set (and we will hit an assert
+is the file handle destructor) when calling file_free.
+We need to set fd to -1 to avoid that. To achieve that we capture and
+return the vfs_stat_fsp failure status while still processing the rest
+of the fd_close logic.
+
+diff --git a/source3/smbd/open.c b/source3/smbd/open.c
+index 0862c956c45..e5309a7be98 100644
+--- a/source3/smbd/open.c
++++ b/source3/smbd/open.c
+@@ -942,7 +942,7 @@ NTSTATUS fd_openat(const struct files_struct *dirfsp,
+
+ NTSTATUS fd_close(files_struct *fsp)
+ {
+-	NTSTATUS status;
++	NTSTATUS stat_status = NT_STATUS_OK;
+ 	int ret;
+
+ 	if (fsp == fsp->conn->cwd_fsp) {
+@@ -950,10 +950,12 @@ NTSTATUS fd_close(files_struct *fsp)
+ 	}
+
+ 	if (fsp->fsp_flags.fstat_before_close) {
+-		status = vfs_stat_fsp(fsp);
+-		if (!NT_STATUS_IS_OK(status)) {
+-			return status;
+-		}
++		/*
++		 * capture status, if failure
++		 * continue close processing
++		 * and return status
++		 */
++		stat_status = vfs_stat_fsp(fsp);
+ 	}
+
+ 	if (fsp->dptr) {
+@@ -975,7 +977,7 @@ NTSTATUS fd_close(files_struct *fsp)
+ 	if (ret == -1) {
+ 		return map_nt_error_from_unix(errno);
+ 	}
+-	return NT_STATUS_OK;
++	return stat_status;
+ }
+
+ /****************************************************************************
diff --git a/debian/patches/series b/debian/patches/series
index fbadf26..716cb55 100644
--- a/debian/patches/series
+++ b/debian/patches/series
@@ -102,3 +102,5 @@ security-202607/security-202607-20.patch
 security-202607/security-202607-21.patch
 security-202607/security-202607-22.patch
 security-202607/security-202607-23.patch

diff --git a/debian/patches/simplify-handling-of-failing-fstat-after-unlinking-file.patch b/debian/patches/simplify-handling-of-failing-fstat-after-unlinking-file.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e941ee0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/simplify-handling-of-failing-fstat-after-unlinking-file.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+Description: smbd: simplify handling of failing fstat() after
+ unlinking file
+Author: Ralph Boehme <slow@samba.org>
+Bug: https://bugzilla.samba.org/show_bug.cgi?id=15527
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/samba/+bug/2166678
+Origin: upstream, https://github.com/samba-team/samba/commit/3634df5d59e9f47345932a00098aead7efe55009
+Last-Update: 2026-09-24
+
+close_remove_share_mode() already called vfs_stat_fsp(), so we can skip the
+fstat() triggered in fd_close() by fsp->fsp_flags.fstat_before_close being true.
+
+This avoids getting an EACCESS error when doing an fstat() on the removed file
+which seems to happen with some FUSE filesystems.
+
+diff --git a/source3/smbd/close.c b/source3/smbd/close.c
+index b42f4d2db71..04e39774950 100644
+--- a/source3/smbd/close.c
++++ b/source3/smbd/close.c
+@@ -603,6 +603,7 @@ static NTSTATUS close_remove_share_mode(files_struct *fsp,
+  	 */
+
+ 	fsp->fsp_flags.delete_on_close = false;
++	fsp->fsp_flags.fstat_before_close = false;
+ 	lck_state.reset_delete_on_close = true;
+
+  done:
+diff --git a/source3/smbd/open.c b/source3/smbd/open.c
+index 3e7a8f45ebd..0862c956c45 100644
+--- a/source3/smbd/open.c
++++ b/source3/smbd/open.c
+@@ -952,20 +952,7 @@ NTSTATUS fd_close(files_struct *fsp)
+ 	if (fsp->fsp_flags.fstat_before_close) {
+ 		status = vfs_stat_fsp(fsp);
+ 		if (!NT_STATUS_IS_OK(status)) {
+-			/*
+-			 * If this is a stream and delete-on-close was set, the
+-			 * backing object (an xattr from streams_xattr) might
+-			 * already be deleted so fstat() fails with
+-			 * NT_STATUS_NOT_FOUND. So if fsp refers to a stream we
+-			 * ignore the error and only bail for normal files where
+-			 * an fstat() should still work. NB. We cannot use
+-			 * fsp_is_alternate_stream(fsp) for this as the base_fsp
+-			 * has already been closed at this point and so the value
+-			 * fsp_is_alternate_stream() checks for is already NULL.
+-			 */
+-			if (fsp->fsp_name->stream_name == NULL) {
+-				return status;
+-			}
++			return status;
+ 		}
+ 	}
